answers.question: Is the property currently compliant for gas safety? Which record do you trust and why?
answers.answer: Yes, today. The compliance record shows a CP12 issued 2025-10-17 and expiring 2026-10-16, with Gas Safe engineer 550123 (matches HeatRight) and a file reference. I trust it over the legacy note ('renewed 2025, all good'), which is an unverified old-agency comment with no dates. It lapses in 6 days if not renewed. The renewal can be done up to 2 months early and keeps the anniversary date.

answers.question: What steps do you take to get access lawfully before expiry?
answers.answer: Opened a job, emailed the tenant asking for times (earlier email and SMS on 25 Sep and 2 Oct went unanswered), asked HeatRight for slots, and will send at least 24h written notice for a confirmed slot. If there is still no reply, I will send a letter and phone the tenant, then escalate to compliance. No forced entry; keys give no right of entry.

answers.question: What do you tell the landlord?
answers.answer: Ben has been told the certificate expires 16 Oct, the tenant has not responded, and we propose HeatRight (his preferred gas contractor). We asked for approval, said a price is pending and that we would call him before anything over £300.
